program: Wingless disjoint-dataset marginal-curve attribution of R16 transfer tie
question: Did the R15 marginal-value asymmetry itself shift on the disjoint transfer dataset, explaining why the frozen R16 curve-guided allocation tied equal allocation?
hypothesis: On the exact R16 disjoint transfer manifest, measure the same frozen per-domain marginal grids used by R15 with the same 15,819 non-target bytes, 256 motifs, 582-byte sealed evaluation, and 872-byte adaptation reservoir. No allocation is selected. For the exact R16 transfer move, define predicted_curve_net_delta = technical_prose gain from 581→726 minus structured gain from 436→581. If this value is <=0, the local marginal curve no longer supports moving 145 bytes from structured to prose and the R16 tie is attributed to curve shift. If it is +1 or +2, attribution is mixed. If it is >2, the marginal curves still predict benefit and the R16 tie instead points to non-additivity/interaction.

successor_if_supported.intent: search for a training-only marginal signal that predicts when originating-dataset allocation curves remain transferable, without selecting policy from heldout outcomes
